source_facts.fact: GOV.UK CIL guidance was updated 17 June 2026 and continues to distinguish charging, liability, relief, collection, spending, appeals and reporting stages.
source_facts.gate: A charging schedule or generic CIL rule is not a parcel liability notice or amount due.

source_facts.fact: Section 106 obligations must meet necessity, direct relationship and fair-and-reasonable scale/kind tests and are distinct from CIL.
source_facts.gate: A policy expectation or formula is not an executed S106 obligation for a parcel.

source_facts.fact: Authorities receiving developer contributions must report CIL and planning obligations at least annually; allocated funds are commitments to infrastructure, not proof of expenditure or delivery.
source_facts.gate: Allocated, received, spent and delivered must remain distinct states.

source_facts.fact: Current viability guidance says application-stage viability assessment is for particular circumstances and the weight given is a decision-maker matter.
source_facts.gate: A viability assessment does not automatically reduce contributions or prove a scheme viable.

source_facts.fact: The January 2026 policy roadmap includes a time-limited route for certain uncontracted affordable homes with defined eligibility and Clearing Service steps.
source_facts.gate: The emergency route is not a general right to renegotiate every S106 agreement.

source_facts.fact: DfE guidance says housing growth should mitigate education infrastructure impacts using local evidence, pupil-yield information and viability-aware contribution planning.
source_facts.gate: Generic pupil yields or national guidance cannot be converted into a parcel contribution without local policy and scheme inputs.

official_measurement_examples.fact: Community Infrastructure Levy guidance shows last update 17 June 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: IFS annual reporting rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: Authorities receiving CIL or S106 contributions must publish infrastructure funding statements at least annually under the reporting framework.

official_measurement_examples.name: IFS allocation semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: Allocated means the authority has decided to commit funds to an infrastructure item or project.

official_measurement_examples.name: S106 statutory tests
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning obligations must be necessary, directly related, and fairly and reasonably related in scale and kind to development.

official_measurement_examples.name: S106 roadmap date status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Roadmap published 28 January 2026 and updated 24 March 2026 includes a time-limited process for qualifying uncontracted affordable homes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Clearing Service London expansion
official_measurement_examples.fact: Homes England collection was updated 28 January 2026 and states the S106 Affordable Housing Clearing Service includes London.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local Plan implementation funding
official_measurement_examples.fact: May 2026 publication reports over £15.7 million issued to local planning authorities under the identified support funding round.

official_measurement_examples.name: Education contribution evidence scope

core_rules: CIL charging schedule is not a parcel liability notice
generic CIL rate is not the final amount due for a specific development
CIL liability depends on chargeable development and applicable calculation rules
CIL relief or exemption must not be assumed without a valid claim and eligibility evidence
CIL exemption eligibility does not prove exemption was successfully claimed
CIL liability notice is distinct from demand notice and payment status
CIL payment is distinct from planning permission implementation
CIL receipt by an authority is not proof the funded infrastructure has been delivered
CIL allocation is not the same as expenditure
CIL expenditure is not proof an infrastructure project is complete
neighbourhood CIL is distinct from the charging authority share
Mayoral CIL must remain distinct from local charging-authority CIL
S106 planning obligation is legally distinct from CIL
S106 agreement is distinct from a planning condition
section 278 highway agreement is distinct from section 106
planning-obligation policy is not an executed agreement
heads of terms are not a completed planning obligation
unilateral undertaking does not bind the authority in the same way as a bilateral agreement
S106 obligation must satisfy the statutory tests for the particular development
formulaic contribution evidence does not remove the need for regulation 122 tests
planning permission subject to S106 is not evidence the agreement has been completed unless confirmed
executed S106 agreement does not prove every trigger has occurred
S106 trigger date is not payment date unless the agreement says so
contribution received is not contribution spent
contribution spent is not infrastructure completed
in-kind contribution must not be treated as cash receipt
monitoring fee is not infrastructure delivery expenditure
IFS is a reporting snapshot and not a live parcel account
IFS financial year must be retained when interpreting figures
IFS allocated amount is a committed funding decision not completed construction
authority monitoring report is not a substitute for the required IFS where IFS duties apply
developer-contribution CSV publication does not prove the underlying agreement remains unmodified
superseded agreement data must not be reported as current without version checks
viability assessment is not automatic permission to reduce policy requirements
viability conclusion depends on inputs assumptions and decision-maker weight
benchmark land value is not parcel market value unless supported by the actual viability evidence
policy-compliant application should not be assumed unviable from generic market conditions
S106 renegotiation is not automatic because affordable units are unsold
2026 time-limited S106 route must retain its eligibility dates and Clearing Service conditions
Clearing Service listing is not a completed sale to a registered provider
education contribution guidance does not create a universal per-dwelling charge
pupil-yield evidence must be matched to local methodology and development mix
central education funding does not automatically replace developer mitigation
plan-making infrastructure evidence is not a parcel planning permission
local-plan implementation grant to an authority is not funding committed to a specific development
future infrastructure intention in an IFS is not guaranteed delivery
NO_DATA must not be converted into no developer contribution liability
no parcel liability contribution balance viability result or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel financial accuracy
